title: Lazarus at the gate (Luke 16:19–31)
hookLine: a rich man never noticed the beggar at his own gate

cards: Things right at your door can become invisible exactly because they're always there: the recycling bin, the neighbor's car, maybe a person sitting against the wall of the corner store you pass every day.
Jesus tells a parable about two men separated by a single gate. One lives behind it in luxury. The other lies just outside it, every day.
One of them has a name in the story. It's not the rich one.

teach.b: Luke paints the rich man in two strokes: clothed in purple and fine linen, feasting sumptuously every day. Purple dye was ruinously expensive, the color of kings.
Then the other man: "And there was a certain beggar, named Lazarus, who lay at his gate, full of sores." He longs for the crumbs from the table, and the dogs come and lick his sores.

teach.h: THE ONLY NAMED MAN JESUS INVENTS.
teach.b: Of all the people Jesus invents for his parables, Lazarus is the only one given a name. Abraham and Moses appear here too, but they come from Scripture.
Later Latin readers called the rich man Dives, but that's just the Latin word for rich. Both men die. Lazarus is carried by angels to Abraham's bosom.
The rich man is in torment, and now he looks up and sees Lazarus. He knows his name.

teach.h: HE KNEW HIS NAME ALL ALONG.
teach.b: He knew it all along. He asks Abraham to send Lazarus with a drop of water, as if Lazarus were still a servant. Abraham answers gently, calling him son, and says a great chaos is now fixed between them.
One more request: send Lazarus to warn my five brothers. Abraham says: they have Moses and the prophets. Let them hear them.
If they won't, they won't believe even if someone rises from the dead. The rich man is never accused of hurting Lazarus, never cruel to him.
His sin is simpler and more common: Lazarus was at his gate every day, and he stepped around him.

teach.h: A BEGGAR, NAMED LAZARUS, AT HIS GATE.
teach.b: The chasm after death is just the gate made permanent.

how: Catholics hear the parable of the rich man and Lazarus at Sunday Mass in the year of Luke's Gospel, and popes, Paul VI and Francis among them, have used it to speak about the rich and the poor in today's world.

practice: Walk in your mind along the route you take every day, front door, street, store, office, the screen you scroll, and ask who is there every day that you've stopped seeing.
Let one person come into focus: someone sitting outside, a lonely neighbor, a coworker who eats alone. If you pray, pray for them, by name if you know it.

wordCard.voice: Lazarus. The poor man with a name, lying every day at the door of a rich man who stepped around him. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Eleazar, God has helped. Lazarus is the Greek form of the name.

carryVoice: Your line: he was at the gate. Every day, a name, right there. Day four hundred seventy-two, in the books.
